items.t: 7-speed automatic shifts harshly or goes into limp mode
items.job: Replace transmission conductor plate (control unit) and program it
items.note: Parts: the plate alone runs about $1,000; a genuine kit for 2010-2011 ML350 lists at about $1,258. One dealer estimate showed 6+ hours of labor (about $2,000 total). Early transmissions may also need a valve body, pushing the bill past $2,000.

items.t: Transmission fluid leaks from the wiring connector
items.job: Replace transmission connector plug adapter and O-rings, top up fluid
items.note: Mercedes bulletin T-B-27.00/48b covers this on all 1998-2005 M-Class with the 5-speed automatic (plug adapter A203 540 00 53). If fluid has already reached the wiring harness or control unit, those repairs cost much more.

items.t: Camshaft adjuster solenoids fail or leak oil
items.job: Replace camshaft adjuster solenoid(s)
items.note: Low is one aftermarket solenoid (about $36; genuine about $66); high is a full set-of-four repair kit (about $281). Labor hours are backed out of YourMechanic's labor charge. YourMechanic: $363-$426 for one solenoid ($395-$586 at a shop or dealer).

items.t: Diesel oil cooler seals leak into the engine valley
items.job: Remove intake and replace oil cooler seals (and cooler if needed)
items.note: Low is the seal and gasket kit (about $50-$120); high adds a new oil cooler (about $157) and filters. Parts supplier ID Parts says an experienced shop needs 8-10 hours. Owners report $1,900-$3,100 total, with dealer quotes above $4,000.

items.t: Crankshaft pulley (harmonic balancer) separates
items.job: Replace crankshaft pulley (harmonic balancer)
items.note: The pulley costs around $100. Labor hours are backed out of shop totals: Mercedes Medic puts a shop or dealer at $350-$700, and YourMechanic quotes $395-$408 ($448-$614 at a shop) for 1998-2002 ML320.

items.t: Door lock actuators fail and lock buttons jump
items.job: Replace door latch and lock actuator (one door)
items.note: Based on YourMechanic, since no parts-plus-labor source was found: $920-$970 for one side door on 1999-2003 ML320 ($1,100-$1,680 at a shop or dealer); a rear hatch is about $476. Price is per door.

items.t: Airmatic air suspension sags and the compressor wears out
items.job: Replace one Airmatic air strut
items.note: Price is per strut. A worn-out compressor adds roughly as much again.

items.t: Balance shaft gear wears and the check engine light comes on
items.job: Replace balance shaft and timing components
items.note: One owner reported a $5,500 estimate; independent Mercedes specialists usually charge less than dealers.

items.t: Engine stalls when hot from a failing crankshaft sensor
items.job: Replace crankshaft position sensor

items.t: Catalytic converters break apart and rattle
items.job: Replace catalytic converter
items.note: Price is for one converter.

items.t: Brake light warning from melted tail lamp sockets
items.job: Replace tail lamp housing or socket
items.note: Engine Patrol puts a lamp housing replacement at upwards of $250.

items.t: Power steering rack leaks and steering gets heavy
items.job: Replace power steering rack and align
items.note: Engine Patrol puts this at upwards of $2,000 when no recall applies.

items.t: Diesel emissions settlement repair and extended warranty
items.job: Emissions software update and parts under the settlement
items.note: Done free by a Mercedes dealer under the emissions settlement.
